mappings.note: Defines a constitution as a nation's body of fundamental law. The goal is about imbibing the values of the Indian Constitution, so it is the natural home; none of its LOs reaches the document as a whole.
Why the original manuscript is kept in a helium-filled case - the care given to the founding document. Constitutional values under the goal.
What a constitution sets out about the structure and powers of government. The goal's institutions clause.
Names the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly. A fact about how the Constitution was made, so the goal.
Fundamental Rights as enforceable against Directive Principles as guidance. A distinction inside the Constitution, so the goal; LO-198 is kept for items where equality itself is the point.
The Constitution as a living document open to amendment. Constitutional values under the goal.
Why a diverse Constituent Assembly mattered. The making of the Constitution, so the goal.

Asks the learner to argue whether equality before the law is actually a fact. That is both the significance of equality (LO-198) and interpreting a real social issue against the right to equality (LO-200).
Why India granted universal adult franchise from the outset. The equal political worth of every citizen, so the equality outcome rather than the general goal.
How the freedom struggle and India's older heritage shaped the Constitution. The making and values of the Constitution, so the goal.
Whether constitutional ideals have been realised and what citizens can do. Civic responsibility under the goal; the ideals named are plural rather than equality alone.
Identifies Fundamental Rights as the basic rights every citizen holds. Constitutional values under the goal.
Accepts vasudhaiva kutumbakam in the Constitution but rejects the claim that it came only from Western philosophy. The sources of constitutional values, so the goal.
Finds the wrongly described constitutional feature. Constitutional structure under the goal.
Rejects the claim that amendments need no parliamentary debate. Constitutional process under the goal.
The artists who illustrated the handwritten Constitution. A fact about the document itself, so the goal.
What fraternity assures in the Preamble. A Preamble value; equality has its own outcome, but fraternity does not, so the goal.
Ireland as the source of the Directive Principles. The borrowing behind the Constitution, so the goal.
Completes 'We, the People of India'. The Preamble's opening claim that authority flows from the people.
France as the source of liberty, equality and fraternity. A question about where the ideals came from, so the goal rather than the equality outcome.
A law discriminating by religion violates the Preamble's guarantee of equality. The item turns on equality, so LO-198.
'Sovereign' in the Preamble. A constitutional term under the goal.
Why members from many regions, professions and social groups mattered in the Assembly. The making of the Constitution, so the goal.
Names the chair of the Drafting Committee. A fact about how the Constitution was written.
Matches constitutional concepts to the countries that inspired them. Sources of the Constitution under the goal.
Accepts that the Constitution contains Directive Principles but rejects the claim that they are immediately enforceable. Constitutional structure under the goal.
Finds the item that is not a Fundamental Duty. Constitutional duties under the goal.
Rejects the claim that everything was borrowed from Britain. The plural sources of the Constitution, so the goal.
The year the Constituent Assembly was formed. A fact about the drafting process.
What 'secular' means for the Indian state. A Preamble value under the goal.
The year Fundamental Duties were added as Part IV-A. Constitutional history under the goal.
Why the Constitution is said to be enacted by the people through their representatives. The source of constitutional authority, so the goal.

A law barring some communities from wells and temples has to be judged against the right to equality - interpreting a concrete social issue by that right, which is LO-200's wording. LO-198 would fit a question about why equality matters in the abstract.
Sorts the Preamble's stated values from one that is not there. Constitutional values under the goal.
Names the calligrapher of the original text. A fact about the document.
'Republic' in the Preamble - an elected rather than hereditary head of state. A constitutional term under the goal.
Enforceable Fundamental Rights against non-justiciable Fundamental Duties. Constitutional structure under the goal.
Matches an article to its Fundamental Right. Constitutional structure; the correct pairing is not specifically the equality article, so the goal rather than LO-198.
Why the Constitution's illustrations show gurukulas and scenes from the epics - anchoring the document in India's heritage. Constitutional values under the goal.
A court affirming flag-flying as part of freedom of expression shows rights being enforced. The right at issue is expression rather than equality, so the goal rather than LO-198.
